newsitem.title: LEBANON: Envoy indicates Syrians hold disappeared Jordanian.
newsitem.headline: Envoy indicates Syrians hold disappeared Jordanian.

text.p: Jordan's ambassador to Lebanon indicated on Monday that a Jordanian executive of a Beirut hotel who disappeared on January 3 after being taken away by unknown men was being held by Syrian security forces.
Ambassador Fakhry Abou Taleb said that Derar al-Karmi, financial controller at the Marriott Hotel, was in the hands of non-Lebanese security forces "concerned with Lebanese security".
This appeared a reference to Syria, Lebanon's main power broker which has 35,000 troops in the country.

"Through my personal contacts and the contacts of the hotel's general manager...we found out that Derar is not in the hands of Lebanese security forces," Abou Taleb told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"According to unofficial information, he is with security forces concerned with security in Lebanon," he added.

Abou Taleb said Karmi, who is of Palestinian origin, was taken from the Marriott on the evening of January 3 by three men in civilian cloths who drove a grey Range Rover with Lebanese registration plates. He said the embassy had identified the ownership of the vehicle.
"Derar whispered to a colleague: 'Mukhabarat (intelligence officers)', before he was taken from his office...," the ambassador said.
Beirut newspapers said on Saturday Karmi was taken by Lebanese security forces on suspicion of links with recent anti-Syrian attacks.

Ad-Diyar daily said he was being questioned over a December 18 machinegun attack on a van carrying Syrian workers in a Christian area north of Beirut in which the driver was killed and a number of passengers wounded.
An-Nahar daily said it was not clear if Karmi was being questioned over the van incident or a December 31 bus bombing in Damascus, the Syrian capital, that killed 11 people.
Abou Taleb said Lebanese authorities had failed to respond to his requests for information about Karmi.
A Lebanese foreign ministry official confirmed on Monday that the ambassador had been in contact and that discussions with him were continuing.
Lebanese judicial authorities have declined to comment on the case, saying they have nothing to do with it.
